audit_method: Same-agent exact comparison against the frozen source, its local definitions, cited propositions, proof dependencies, language-tag branches and semantic countercases within that revision. No claim about current upstream master is made.

corrections.finding: The phrase the proof of is preceded by a second definite article.
corrections.handling: Removed the duplicated article in translation and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The intended noun phrase is the proof of the completeness theorem; no mathematical content changes.

corrections.finding: The adjectival token denumerable carries a plural suffix before singular model.
corrections.handling: Rendered denumerable as an adjective modifying one structure and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The construction supplies one finite or denumerable model for each satisfiable set.

corrections.finding: Condition (b) requires a decision only for atomic sentences, while the definition immediately below requires a decision for every sentence.
corrections.handling: Removed the atomic-only restriction so the outline matches the complete-set definition and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The next definition and the later Lindenbaum construction enumerate every sentence, and the Truth Lemma needs completeness at compound formulas too.

corrections.finding: The quantifier all is followed by singular sentence.
corrections.handling: Used the intended plural phrase all sentences and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The claim ranges over the entire set Gamma.

corrections.finding: The quotient classes are said to collect terms that the original set Gamma requires equal, although the formal equivalence relation is defined from the completed extension Gamma-star.
corrections.handling: Used Gamma-star as the theory controlling equality classes and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The later definition sets t approximately t-prime exactly when the identity sentence belongs to Gamma-star.

corrections.finding: One branch omits the argument x_n from A_n inside a universal formula.
corrections.handling: Restored A_n(x_n), matching the adjacent branch and definition, and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The enumerated formula is A_n(x_n), and all neighbouring occurrences in the reductio use that open formula.

corrections.finding: The explanatory existential-instance clause is gated by prvAll rather than prvEx.
corrections.handling: Changed the clause gate to prvEx, matching the formal proposition below, and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The corresponding tagged item prop:saturated-instances uses prvEx for the existential clause.

corrections.finding: The proof selects the largest index contributed by an arbitrary finite subset without handling the empty subset, for which no such index exists.
corrections.handling: Separated the empty subset case before selecting a largest index and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The empty subset is consistent trivially; every nonempty finite subset contributes a finite nonempty set of indices with a maximum.

corrections.finding: Four quantifier-case occurrences say terms without the closed-term restriction required by the cited term-model and saturation propositions.
corrections.handling: Restricted all four occurrences to closed terms and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The cited propositions quantify over closed terms, and B(t) must be a sentence for membership in the complete sentence set.

corrections.finding: The universal induction case ends with forall x A(x), though the case assumption identifies A with forall x B(x).
corrections.handling: Restored B as the quantified matrix and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The induction-case header is A ident forall x B(x), and every preceding satisfaction and membership step uses B(t).

corrections.finding: The first compound function term contains a duplicated comma after t_{i+1}.
corrections.handling: Removed the stray comma and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The parallel term on the right and the surrounding n-ary argument list contain one separator at that position.

corrections.finding: The discussion introduces an alternative representative t-prime but states non-satisfaction for R(t), repeating the original representative.
corrections.handling: Used R(t-prime) in the alternative-representative premise and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The claimed conflict concerns whether the same equivalence class receives different membership results under representatives t and t-prime.

corrections.finding: The first Truth Lemma equivalence is attributed only to the quotient-structure definition, omitting the lemma that computes term values as equivalence classes.
corrections.handling: Cited the value lemma together with the identity interpretation and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: Satisfaction of t=t-prime compares their values; lem:val-in-termmodel-factored identifies those values with the displayed equivalence classes.

corrections.finding: The theorem calls both Gamma and A sentences, although Gamma is a set of sentences and A is one sentence.
corrections.handling: Stated the two variable types explicitly and added an adjacent keyed note.

mathematical_delta.removed: Gamma and A both typed as sentences
mathematical_delta.added: Gamma a sentence set; A a sentence

corrections.controlling_evidence: Both clauses quantify over finite subsets of Gamma and use A as the entailed sentence.

corrections.finding: The sentence says there are models followed by a satisfaction formula rather than a structure, and it reuses M from the finite-subset construction.
corrections.handling: Introduced a fresh structure N and separately stated that N satisfies Gamma union Delta, then added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: Compactness yields existence of a structure satisfying the whole set; the preceding M is a fixed model used to build finite expansions M-prime.

corrections.finding: The phrase for all the sentences ... have k<K is grammatically malformed and obscures the scope of the index bound.
corrections.handling: Stated that every relevant sentence occurring in Delta-zero has index k below K and added an adjacent keyed note.

mathematical_delta.added: explicit universal scope over members of Delta-zero

corrections.controlling_evidence: A finite subset contains finitely many indexed inequalities, so a common strict upper bound K exists for their indices.

corrections.finding: The proof chooses the largest n represented in an arbitrary finite Delta-prime without handling the empty set.
corrections.handling: Separated the empty Delta-prime case before selecting the maximum and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: Any finite structure satisfying Lambda-prime handles the empty case; a nonempty finite index set has a maximum.

corrections.finding: The source says that changing two cited propositions makes the Truth Lemma proof go through, but its falsity, truth and negation cases also invoke consistency directly.
corrections.handling: Added the finite-satisfiability arguments establishing false is absent, true is present and negation membership complements membership, then added an adjacent keyed note.

mathematical_delta.removed: claim that two citation substitutions suffice
mathematical_delta.added: finite-satisfiability replacements in three direct-consistency cases

corrections.controlling_evidence: Each contrary membership pattern would form an unsatisfiable finite subset of size one or two, contradicting finite satisfiability.

corrections.finding: The general first-order compactness proof constructs only the plain term model and cites a Truth Lemma explicitly restricted to formulas without identity.
corrections.handling: Added the quotient term-model case, including finite-satisfiability arguments for well-definedness, and added an adjacent keyed note.

mathematical_delta.added: quotient term model and identity Truth Lemma adaptation

corrections.controlling_evidence: The cited simple Truth Lemma excludes identity, while the theorem is stated for the full FOL profile; the identity chapter supplies the required quotient construction.

corrections.finding: The proof bounds the constructed domain by terms of the original language L, although the completeness construction first adds Henkin constants and uses terms of the expanded language L-prime.
corrections.handling: Used the expanded language L-prime, whose term set remains countable, and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The Henkin expansion precedes the term-model construction, and its fresh constants occur among the closed terms forming that model's domain.

corrections.finding: The FOL-only term-value block supplies only two of iftag's three required arguments.
corrections.handling: Added the required empty false branch and an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: open-logic-selective.sty defines iftag with three arguments; without the empty third argument TeX consumes the following conditional token as the false branch.

corrections.finding: The FOL-only clause naming the saturation reference supplies no third argument to iftag.
corrections.handling: Added the required empty false branch and an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: open-logic-selective.sty defines iftag with three arguments; the adjacent prose resumes after the conditional and is not an alternate branch.
